markdown_report:
The first experiment should test a **context-conditioned soft-reset GRU**. This preserves GRU4Rec while targeting stale interests and weak connections to current activity. Improvement remains a hypothesis requiring pinned validation.

### Insights and framework

Three baseline insights guide selection. First, users reject revived interests and weakly connected media; selective retention might improve current-intent representation, but cannot establish compatibility or redundancy. Second, Electronics’ 9.7% wrong-rank rate and 0.0265 lower-decile margin motivate investigating ambiguous contexts; these training diagnostics do not establish generalization. Third, collapse scores near 0.5 indicate approximately zero mean cosine similarity, providing no support for collapse regularization.

Three literature insights define complementary directions. MTAM [1] motivates recurrent gating, without validating this construction. GRU4Rec [2] supports competitive-negative objectives, although unobserved relevant items can become negatives. Recformer [3] motivates recommendation-specific text representations, without establishing benefits for from-scratch GRU text fusion. Standard GRUs already condition gates on input and state [4]; the proposal adds attenuation, not new information.

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Compatible hypothesis | Principal uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| State retention | MTAM temporal gates | Item/state-conditioned soft reset | Redundant gating; useful history loss |
| Ranking objective | GRU4Rec BPR-max | Regularized competitive-negative learning | False negatives; objective dependence |
| Item representation | Recformer text integration | Jointly trained title residual | Broad lexical shortcuts |

### Candidate assessments

Scores are originality / future potential / user alignment / model alignment / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. Each dimension includes a positive and negative reason.

- **Soft-reset GRU: 3/6/7/6/5.** Originality: distinct carry attenuation; established gating. Potential: reusable retention control; no new context. User alignment: targets stale interests and weak recent connections; cannot verify current need. Model alignment: tests contextual ambiguity; gains unmeasured. Difficulty: localized architecture; recurrent loops and parity checks add cost.
- **BPR-max: 2/6/5/8/3.** Originality: useful transfer; established objective. Potential: inexpensive discrimination; limited architectural insight. User alignment: challenges distractors; lacks explicit intent modeling. Model alignment: emphasizes competitive negatives; margins need not improve HR@10. Difficulty: localized change; collision masking requires care.
- **Title residual: 4/7/7/5/5.** Originality: constrained adaptation; established fusion. Potential: shares sparse-item supervision; noisy metadata. User alignment: supplies artist/purpose connections; overlap cannot prove fit. Model alignment: may clarify items; may amplify confusion. Difficulty: simple pooling; vocabulary and serialization add work.

### Selected experiment

At 0% progress, retain soft-reset GRU as a bounded hypothesis addressing **revived older interests** and **weak connections to recent activity**, plus Electronics’ weak separation. Compute q=g⊙h before the ordinary GRU update; this attenuates gates, candidate construction, and carry [4]. Initialize zero gate weights and bias logit(0.99), recognizing this only approximates the baseline and may slow gate learning.

Preserve baseline loss, sampling, padding behavior, diagnostic interfaces, and predictor architecture. First verify exact g≡1 parity, then profile training cost. Prioritize baseline versus learned gate; defer constant-gate and parameter-matched controls unless budget permits. Select solely by fixed macro validation HR@10. Log comparisons and paired user outcomes when available; uncertainty intervals remain exploratory because adaptive validation selection creates optimism [5]. Sampled HR does not establish full-catalog quality [6].

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598), [2](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf), [3](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/kdd23b.pdf), [4](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.3555), [5](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html), [6](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

idea.description: Add a jointly trained, item-and-state-conditioned soft-retention gate before each GRU4Rec recurrent update. Retain the supplied baseline’s scoring head, objective, negative sampling, and padding semantics for the first controlled experiment. Treat the gate as a modest architectural hypothesis rather than a novel source of contextual information.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies revived older interests and recommendations weakly connected to recent activity. Selective retention might reduce these two failures by suppressing irrelevant accumulated state while preserving coherent preferences. Electronics’ 0.0265 lower-decile margin, 9.7% wrong-rank rate, and 14.82% small-margin rate motivate testing context discrimination. A standard GRU already uses input- and state-dependent gates, so this extra gate may be redundant. It cannot establish equipment compatibility, redundant functionality, actual current need, or media mood from interaction IDs alone. Embedding-collapse regularization is not motivated by the supplied near-zero mean cosine similarities.
idea.implementation_notes:
Architecture: for each existing GRU layer, compute g_t = sigmoid(W_e e_t + W_h h_previous + b), q_t = g_t * h_previous, and h_t = GRUCell(e_t, q_t). Preserve the baseline’s layer count, width, transformations, scoring head, and dropout placement. This changes all recurrent computations, including the carry path, rather than merely modifying the ordinary reset gate. Initialize gate projection weights to zero and b = log(99), so g starts at 0.99. This is approximate baseline preservation: repeated attenuation can still materially shorten memory, and sigmoid saturation can slow learning. Implement an explicit g≡1 switch for correctness checks; finite sigmoid bias cannot produce exact identity.

Baseline equivalence: preserve the supplied model’s actual padding behavior. Zero padding embeddings alone do not prevent recurrent bias updates. If the baseline freezes hidden states on padding, freeze every layer; if it updates them, retain that behavior for this controlled comparison. Do not silently introduce padding masking as a second intervention. With dropout disabled, copy weight_ih_l{k}, weight_hh_l{k}, bias_ih_l{k}, and bias_hh_l{k} into corresponding cells, preserving PyTorch gate order and its reset-after-recurrent-affine candidate equation. Compare exact-identity-gate timestep outputs, final states, scores, losses, and mapped gradients against the baseline using dtype-appropriate tolerances, initially atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5 for float32. Include mixed-length and all-padding cases. Restore the baseline’s between-layer dropout afterward; matching seeds does not guarantee identical dropout masks across implementations.

Interfaces and inference: retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), family-specific sample_batch, and view.model as the actual trained nn.Module. For left-padded histories, read the greatest index with a nonzero item, never count-1; preserve the baseline’s documented all-padding fallback. Compute retention only from the observed prefix and prior hidden state, never from the shifted target. Serialize architecture flags, layer configuration, gate parameters, and padding behavior with the checkpoint, and update the embedded predictor writer to instantiate the identical network. Verify checkpoint reload reproduces scores. Each category must load exactly one independently trained checkpoint; no averaging, score fusion, or independently fitted auxiliary predictors.

Diagnostics: retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and metric_definitions. Keep the existing margin and embedding probes compatible with B x L outputs. Add optional measured gate mean, near-zero/near-one fractions, and summaries by history length, with explicit definitions. Disable dropout and restore the previous training mode around diagnostic measurements. Do not invent missing metadata categories, review content, compatibility labels, or simulator traits. No timestamps or metadata are required for this initial variant.

Experimental control: start from the supplied corrected baseline configuration, retaining its optimizer, loss, sampling, learning rate, regularization, and stopping policy. Change only the gate and the mechanically necessary recurrence implementation. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four category routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and exactly 200 batches per executed epoch. Preserve the supplied SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200 despite the GRU family. Train categories sequentially on one GPU. Select checkpoint epochs using the unchanged validation rule and select the proposal using only the pinned equal-weight four-category macro HR@10.

Budget and controls: profile representative full forward/backward/optimizer steps after warmup with CUDA synchronization, including the longest sequence shape. Include validation, diagnostics, and any compilation in the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Estimate remaining cost as the sum of category step times times 200 times planned epochs, plus measured overhead. Use eager execution first; attempt compilation only if measured savings justify compilation cost. The first scientific contrast is corrected baseline versus learned gate. Exact g≡1 is a correctness control. If budget remains, investigate a learned constant-vector gate and a parameter-matched wider GRU; input-only, hidden-only, and zero-bias controls are secondary. Without these controls, do not attribute any improvement specifically to context-dependent resetting rather than added capacity or regularization.

Evidence and overfitting: log every attempted configuration and validation comparison. Report category HR@10 alongside macro HR@10 without introducing a second selection objective. If the unchanged host exposes paired per-user hit outcomes, report category discordances and a stratified paired-bootstrap interval for the macro difference, resampling user pairs within each category. Do not modify the evaluator to obtain additional metrics. One extra hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. Such intervals omit retraining and candidate-sampling variability and do not correct adaptive search optimism. Shared tokens or observed popularity can become shortcuts in alternative ideas; the selected gate can instead overfit recurring IDs and short contexts. Track retention saturation and history-length sensitivity as diagnostics, not new tuning objectives. Improvements in margins do not demonstrate validation improvement, and sampled validation HR does not establish full-catalog utility. Treat user-facing benefits as hypotheses until observed; use only host-provided validation and the authorized training-user simulator, never hidden test files or other trials.
idea.pseudocode:
class SoftResetGRU:
    initialize_from_baseline_configuration():
        preserve_layers_width_transforms_dropout_and_scoring()
        for layer in layers:
            gate_input_weight[layer] = 0
            gate_hidden_weight[layer] = 0
            gate_bias[layer] = log(99)

    log2feats(sequence, exact_identity_gate=False):
        states = baseline_initial_states(batch_size)
        outputs = []
        for t in range(sequence_length):
            valid = sequence[:, t] != 0
            x = baseline_input_transform(item_emb(sequence[:, t]))
            for layer in layers:
                previous = states[layer]
                if exact_identity_gate:
                    retention = ones_like(previous)
                else:
                    retention = sigmoid(
                        gate_input[layer](x)
                        + gate_hidden[layer](previous)
                        + gate_bias[layer]
                    )
                proposed = gru_cell[layer](x, retention * previous)
                states[layer] = apply_supplied_baseline_padding_semantics(
                    previous, proposed, valid
                )
                x = states[layer]
                if layer_is_not_final:
                    x = baseline_between_layer_dropout(x)
            outputs.append(baseline_output_at_timestep(x, valid))
        return baseline_output_transform(stack(outputs, dim=1))

    predict_score(features, items):
        return baseline_scoring_head(features, items)

# Before training: no external checkpoints or other-trial artifacts.
# Use disposable same-configuration modules for equivalence verification.
copy_GRU_parameters_to_cells_including_both_biases()
disable_dropout()
assert_identity_gate_outputs_states_scores_losses_gradients_match_baseline()
assert_mixed_length_and_all_padding_behavior_matches_baseline()
profile_representative_training_steps_and_budget()

for category in FOUR_FIXED_CATEGORIES:
    seed_training(42)  # Reset after profiling/verification.
    model = SoftResetGRU(supplied_baseline_configuration)
    for epoch in range(configured_epochs_at_most_200):
        for batch_index in range(200):
            sequence, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch()
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positive, negative)
            unchanged_baseline_optimizer_step(loss)
        follow_unchanged_validation_and_checkpoint_selection_policy()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint_with_complete_architecture_configuration()
    verify_matching_predictor_reload_scores()

# Predictor keeps all four routes, loading one checkpoint for each category.
# For each nonempty left-padded sequence:
# last_index = max(where(sequence != 0, position, -1))
# Gather last_index; use the supplied fallback for an all-padding sequence.
# Compare proposals only through pinned macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: The extra gate attenuates the carry path and every recurrent computation, creating a specific, testable adaptation to the supplied stale-interest diagnosis.
originality.negative: Input- and state-conditioned gating is established, including within standard GRUs. The proposal adds no new contextual information, and structural difference alone does not establish novelty.

future_potential.positive: A controlled improvement could motivate interpretable retention analysis and later incorporation of observed historical time gaps within a single GRU network.
future_potential.negative: Benefits remain unmeasured, may reflect extra capacity, and cannot establish compatibility or current need. Unnecessary attenuation can erase useful long-term preferences.

code_difficulty.positive: The mathematical modification requires only two projections and a sigmoid per recurrent layer, without new data or pretrained assets.
code_difficulty.negative: Cell-loop parity, multilayer dropout, padding semantics, gradient checks, runtime budgeting, and synchronized predictor serialization make reliable implementation moderately difficult.

related_work.title: MTAM: temporal gating for sequential recommendation
contributions: Introduces temporal gating in recurrent modeling to represent short-term intent.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed item-and-state-conditioned attenuation.
Does not establish that hard resets or extra gates improve this benchmark.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Develops ranking objectives including BPR-max that emphasize high-scoring negatives.
Provides a compatible alternative direction for improving GRU4Rec discrimination.
limitations: Does not establish superiority under the pinned four-category protocol.
Competitive negatives may include unobserved relevant items.

related_work.title: Recformer
contributions: Suggests shared textual signals can transfer preference information between items.
limitations: Its Transformer architecture and pretraining recipe are outside this experiment.
Does not establish benefits for title pooling trained from scratch with GRU4Rec.

related_work.title: Empirical Evaluation of Gated Recurrent Neural Networks on Sequence Modeling
contributions: Describes GRU reset and update mechanisms.
Provides precedent for parameter-controlled recurrent comparisons.
limitations: Does not evaluate the proposed extra retention gate or this recommendation benchmark.
Standard gating already uses the same input and hidden-state information.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Specifies recurrent equations, parameter layout, multilayer behavior, and dropout placement.
limitations: API equivalence does not guarantee matching dropout realizations or runtime.
Padding semantics must be checked against the supplied implementation.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRUCell documentation
contributions: Specifies cell equations and both bias vectors.
Supports explicit recurrent implementation of the proposed gate.
limitations: Requires explicit timestep and layer loops.
Does not provide sequence-level multilayer dropout automatically.

related_work.title: Recurrent Highway Networks
contributions: Provides precedent for gate initialization favoring carry behavior.
limitations: Does not validate logit(0.99) initialization for this multiplicative GRU gate.
Near-open retention does not exactly preserve baseline computation.

related_work.title: PyTorch benchmark guidance
contributions: Supports measuring full-step costs before committing the search budget.
limitations: Microbenchmarks alone omit validation, diagnostics, and compilation overhead.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit finite validation data.
limitations: Does not supply a task-specific correction for this adaptive search.
Paired uncertainty analyses do not remove selection bias.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics, including model ordering.
limitations: Does not change the required pinned selection metric.
Does not establish whether a particular proposed model will improve.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Supports category-stratified paired uncertainty analysis when per-user outcomes are available.
limitations: Stratified macro resampling requires preserving category structure explicitly.
Intervals omit retraining variability and adaptive selection bias.
